findings.description: The bucket has no ACL set explicitly and is commented as public, with no encryption, versioning, or access logging configured, exposing customer data to unauthorized access and tampering.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including sensitive customer data) are not encrypted at rest.
No versioning block is configured, allowing data to be overwritten or deleted without recovery, weakening data integrity protections in case of accidental or malicious deletion.

A customer master data file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded into the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is publicly accessible and unencrypted, exposing sensitive customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
No versioning block is configured for the financials bucket, risking permanent loss or unauthorized overwrite of financial records.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the operations bucket, so stored data is not encrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the data_science bucket, leaving data unencrypted at rest despite having logging and versioning enabled.
